newsitem.title: USA: Mesa says two units sued by United.
newsitem.headline: Mesa says two units sued by United.

text.p: Mesa Air Group Inc said United Airlines had filed suit against its units Mesa Airlines and WestAir arising from a dispute over markets operated by Mesa in Los Angeles.

In a statement, Mesa said United wants to transfer markets currently operated by Mesa and WestAir to Skywest Airlines, which currently serves the Los Angeles and Salt Lake City hubs as a Delta Airlines code-sharing partner.
Mesa Air and United are code-sharing partners.
Mesa said that of the 16 markets operated by Mesa and WestAir in Los Angeles, United intends to grant eight to Skywest Airlines.
Mesa Air said it believes that its two units have exclusive contract rights to the use of the United Express code in those markets.

It said it has not been formally served court papers, but has received a copy of the complaint. It said the suit asks the court to interpret the existing United Airlines-Mesa Airlines/West Air contracts and determine each party's rights regarding the Los Angeles markets.
Mesa Air declined further comment, saying the litigation was pending.
It noted, however, that it and its units "continue to engage in negotiations in an effort to seek a mutually agreeable resolution to the issues involving the Los Angeles markets."
The Mesa group serves 167 cities in 30 states and the District of Columbia.
